title: LibUsdOracle 1e24/price inversion can DoS via division-by-zero only when price feed returns 0
description: getUsdPrice and getTokenPriceFromExternal divide 1e24 by an oracle price (uint256(1e24).div(LibChainlinkOracle.getTokenPrice(...)) at L120-127; uint256(1e24).div(tokenPrice) at L64). The WETH/WSTETH branches in getUsdPrice guard the 0 case (L52,L57) and the external generic branch guards it (L63), but the encodeType 0x01 branch (L120-127) divides by LibChainlinkOracle.getTokenPrice directly with NO zero-guard. Since LibChainlinkOracle is contractually allowed to return 0 on a broken/frozen feed, a frozen Chainlink feed for a 0x01-registered token causes 1e24/0 to revert instead of returning the 0 sentinel that getUsdPrice's other branches use. (deep-trace DT-007 rated this Medium; downgraded to Low here: the affected path is the chainlink-impl token branch, which the current live wells do not traverse, and the consumer LibWell.getRatiosAndBeanIndex/LibWellMinting wraps failures gracefully only when a 0 is returned, not when the call reverts.)
impact: For a token registered with the chainlink (0x01) oracle implementation, a frozen/broken feed makes getUsdPrice revert (1e24/0) instead of returning 0. Callers that expected the documented 0-sentinel graceful path (e.g. minting success=false) instead get a revert, which can propagate to DoS the calling flow during a feed outage. Low because the live BEAN:WETH/WSTETH wells route through the explicitly-guarded WETH/WSTETH branches, not this one.

ite.intent: Return 0 on feed failure so callers degrade gracefully (per the file's 'returns 0 rather than reverting' contract).
ite.technique: Unguarded division 1e24/price in the 0x01 branch where price can legitimately be 0.
ite.evasion: The sibling branches all guard 0, so the one unguarded division is easy to miss.

ice_chain.consumer_action: reverts during a feed outage instead of degrading to success=false
